analysis:
The PR is a release bump to 0.10.10. It changes CHANGELOG.md (head lines 11-39: a new v0.10.10 candidate section and a retitled v0.10.9 section), removes changelog.d/feature-waitlists.md, bumps docs/operations/provider-release.md, and sets ProviderCore.version from "0.10.9" to "0.10.10" (provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/ProviderCore.swift line 8). No change to protocol, attestation, key handling, encryption, cache storage or privilege paths is visible, so no regression against T-041, T-052, T-054, TB-011, TB-012, TB-013 or TB-014 was found. The replayed patch units confirm that the changelog fragment and the changelog entry carry the same text.

The changelog describes waitlist gating for new `darkbloom sandbox setup` and new two-Mac cluster pairs. It says a coordinator without waitlists lets setup go on as before. That fail-open fallback is a product rollout policy, not a threat-model control. Approval is coordinator-owned and platform-side, so enforcement is outside the supplied evidence. The waitlist client and coordinator-contract code that the notes describe was not supplied: `darkbloom waitlist`, the setup gates, and the claim that joining sends nothing about the Mac. Several source passes flagged this as an unverified contract. The omitted 53 replay units may contain it. If it ships in this PR, a later pass should check the following.
- The waitlist check does not replace the TB-013 installer controls or the TB-014 owner confirmation and administrator prompt.
- The waitlist HTTP calls use the authenticated, issuer-bound coordinator channel (A-008).
- Coordinator responses are treated as untrusted.
- The fail-open path triggers only when the coordinator reports no waitlist feature, and not on errors or unreachability.

The release-doc edit drops pairs on 0.10.8 from the 64-approval catalog room. The document states this as a deliberate availability trade-off (A-018), not a security regression. scripts/check-release-version.sh and the release workflows were not supplied, so the match between the tag and the version, and the documented secret scoping, are unverified. No findings; deeper review is advisable only for the unseen waitlist code.
